source.title: Generalization by design: Shortcuts to Generalization in Deep Learning

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a random-label fit and chance-level test accuracy on MNIST, while using the result to discuss generalization; it does not present an explicit replication of the original study's full protocol.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports the authors' MNIST network reaching zero training error with random labels and approximately 10% test accuracy. The text does not state the architecture details or whether training hyperparameters were unchanged. Other random-label statements cite prior work or are theoretical discussion, not additional results.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 reports the authors' own MNIST convolutional-network experiment: random labels are fitted to zero training error with approximately 10% test accuracy. This uses the original claim's basic method and measures, although the training protocol is insufficiently specified to verify unchanged hyperparameters.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but understates the paper's main conclusion. The authors propose a geometric account of generalization through bounded spectral products and introduce structural generalization layers using skip connections or dropout. Their experiments report improved generalization, especially on CIFAR10. Random-label memorization is an introductory demonstration; noisy-regression experiments motivate their argument that vanilla SGD alone does not ensure generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper reports a random-label MNIST result and chance-level test accuracy, but Figure 1 focuses on weight distributions and does not specify the full training protocol or establish unchanged hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports eventual overfitting of noisy polynomial regression by vanilla-SGD networks of several depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vanilla SGD does not prevent eventual overfitting of noisy regression targets. These snapshots do not separately measure learning of signal and noise as V6 requires.

record.problems: Figure 1 gives limited model and training details and no uncertainty or repeated-run information. The random-label training setup is referred to as described in prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional random-label results are reported. Figure 2 concerns noisy polynomial regression rather than random image-label fitting.

untested.parts: Whether architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged between true-label and random-label training; the precise stochastic-gradient training protocol.
Relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test-error trajectories across intermediate fractions of label corruption.
Random-label fitting under weight decay, dropout and augmentation, and true-label generalization after removing these regularizers.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy labels; separate learning trajectories for signal and noise.

record.verdict_notes: The statement that sufficiently enforced geometric constraints would make random-label solutions unreachable is not an additional measured random-label result. It does not directly test V5's claims about conventional weight decay, dropout and augmentation.

versions.untested_parts: Whether architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged; exact model details; whether test error was measured over repeated runs.
